text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — hit a weird propagation bug in the Python SDK observability when using FastAPI BackgroundTasks and asyncio.create_task. X-Request-ID reaches middleware but inside background thread/task the request id is gone. Minimal repro below.

Noah Patel: Which SDK version?

Maria Chen: redwood-sdk==0.9.2. Repro:
```py
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks, Request
from redwood_sdk.observability import ObservabilityMiddleware, set_request_id_from_headers
app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(ObservabilityMiddleware)

@app.post('/work')
async def work(req: Request, bg: BackgroundTasks):
    set_request_id_from_headers(req.headers)
    def bg_job(rid):
        # prints None
        print('bg job rid=', rid)
    bg.add_task(bg_job, getattr(req.state, 'request_id', None))
    return {'ok': True}
```
curl -H 'X-Request-ID: abc-123' -X POST localhost:8000/work

Susan Li: ContextVars don't cross threadpools/create_task automatically. FastAPI/Starlette BackgroundTasks uses a threadpool, and asyncio.create_task needs context propagation.

Ryan Morgan: Reproduced internally. ObservabilityMiddleware stores request id in a contextvar. We don't currently patch asyncio.create_task or thread executors.

Maria Chen: Also saw that an HTTPX async call inside handler had the right id, but inside create_task() the id was None. BackgroundTasks worse because it's in a worker thread and throws when code assumes a string.

Jon Kline: Request: add a small helper to the SDK to instrument task creation (opt-in) and a helper to copy context to thread executor. Something like instrument_asyncio_tasks() and bridge_context_to_thread(fn). Also add typed callables for middleware hooks so editors can autocomplete.

Noah Patel: Also would love an example FastAPI app in examples/ that demonstrates OTEL + request id propagation patterns (in-request, pass-arg, instrumented tasks, thread bridge). Saved me an hour.

Ryan Morgan: There's an open branch with an AsyncTask wrapper and a bind_context util: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/418. It adds an option to ObservabilityMiddleware: auto_propagate_tasks (opt-in). CI flaky on Windows.

Maria Chen: Tried the branch — create_task propagation improved but BackgroundTasks still loses it because of threadpool. Stack: AttributeError when trying to call .startswith on None.

Susan Li: Workaround: capture rid = get_request_id() and pass explicitly into background fn. For thread executors we can provide copy_context_to_thread(fn, *args, **kwargs) which wraps the function with contextvars.copy_context().run(fn, *args, **kwargs).

Ryan Morgan: Plan: update PR to include docs + FastAPI example under examples/fastapi-observability, add bridge helper for thread-based executors, and add type hints for middleware hooks (suggested signature: Callable[[Mapping[str, str], Optional[str]], None] or async variant). Will also add small note about behaviour differences across Python versions and async frameworks.

Jon Kline: For typing I recommend a simple Protocol: ObservabilityHook = Callable[[dict, str], Coroutine[Any, Any, None]] or sync variant. Keep runtime checks minimal.

ci-bot: build #418 — failing on windows pytest test_observability::test_task_propagation (flaky).

Noah Patel: I'll test the branch on my mac/linux boxes and try to reproduce the windows flake. If you want, I can paste a tiny example into examples/ when CI is green. :thumbsup: 

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone — good to see actionable plan. Quick doc request: add an "observability patterns" checklist for common frameworks (FastAPI, Flask, Celery, plain asyncio) so teams don't reimplement the same hacks. :eyes:
